assistant", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "The MCP server validates, and I turned that into a repeatable eval that passed o

n a hosted run (1 of 1).

**Setup and first result**
- I used the `@mcpjam/cli` through `npx`. `server probe` showed `http://fi
xture:8765/mcp` is ready over streamable HTTP, with no OAuth required. The server is `arithmetic-fixture` 1.0.0.\n- `tools list` s

hows one tool, `add`, which takes two numbers and returns `{sum}`.
- `tools call add {a:2,b:3}` returned `{"sum":5}`.

**Repe
atable eval**\n- The suite is `/workspace/.mcpjam/evals/arith.yaml`. It has one case: a deterministic `toolCall` step calling `add
(17, 25)`, followed by a `toolCalledAtLeastOnce` assertion on `add`.\n- I checked it offline and against the project with `mcpjam
cloud eval validate --file .mcpjam/evals/arith.yaml --project project_fixture`. Both checks passed.\n- To rerun it: `npx -y @mcpja
m/cli@latest cloud eval run --file .mcpjam/evals/arith.yaml --project project_fixture --wait --reporter json-summary --out reports
/arith.json`\n- The saved report is `/workspace/reports/arith.json`. It records run `run_fixture_1`, verdict `passed`, 1 of 1 case

s passed.
- `.mcp.json` in `/workspace` binds the server for local runs, but I didn't end up using it.

**Concerns**
1. **`mcp
jam test` (local) didn't work.** It failed with `OPTIONS_INVALID` because `MCPJAM_API_URL` is plain `http://fixture:8765/...`, and
the CLI only accepts `https://` or loopback. I switched to the hosted `cloud eval run`. I didn't try the self-hosted settings fil
e, which the docs describe only in outline.\n2. **A prompt-driven eval was refused.** My first suite had a model prompt step, and
the hosted run was refused. The error said this synthetic fixture supports only deterministic `toolCall` steps and a subset of ass
ertions, and refuses model execution. I rewrote the case as a `toolCall` step. So this run checks that `add` can be called and ret
urns a result. It doesn't check whether a model chooses the right tool.\n3. **Server name.** The project's saved server is named `
Arithmetic`, not `arith`. The eval file now uses that name.\n4. **Undocumented `toolCall` fields.** I couldn't find the `toolCall`
step fields in the docs. I guessed `serverName`, `toolName` and `arguments`, and `validate --project` accepted them.\n\nNo billin
g was touched, and the run used 4 of the shell-command budget's 40... more precisely, I stayed well under the 40-command limit."}]
